concepts.def: Caused by Earth's rotation on its axis.
Caused by the tilt of Earth's axis.
From the changing sunlit portion we see.
Solar and lunar eclipses from alignment of Sun, Earth, Moon.
Caused mainly by the Moon's gravity.

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Lunar Disc — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

The Lunar Disc brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with The Lunar Disc.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Approximate length of a synodic month?
options: 27.3 days
29.5 days
30.0 days
31.0 days

mcqs.q: Phase when the lit side faces away from Earth?
options: Full Moon
New Moon
First quarter
Gibbous

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a solar and a lunar eclipse?
options: Clouds passing over cause the phases.
They are the same event.
In a solar eclipse the Moon hides the Sun; in a lunar eclipse Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
A solar eclipse is when the Moon simply disappears.

mcqs.q: Does the Moon produce its own light?
options: Earth's shadow causes the phases.
The Moon glows with its own light.
A solar eclipse is when the Moon simply disappears.
No - it reflects sunlight, and phases show how much of the lit half we can see.

mcqs.q: Are Moon phases caused by Earth's shadow?
options: Clouds passing over cause the phases.
Yes, the phases are Earth's shadow on the Moon.
No - phases depend on the Moon's position relative to the Sun and Earth, not Earth's shadow.
Earth's shadow causes the phases.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Full Moon”?
options: Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “New Moon”?
options: Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Waxing / waning”?
options: Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Synodic month”?
options: Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Last quarter”?
options: Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.
Waxing = increasing lit fraction; waning = decreasing lit fraction.
Phase when the Moon is between Earth and the Sun; the lit side faces away from Earth.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “First quarter”?
options: Left half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, three weeks after New Moon.
Time between successive same phases (e.g., New Moon to New Moon): 29.5 days.
Earth is between Sun and Moon; the entire near side appears lit.
Right half of the Moon (Northern Hemisphere) is lit, one week after New Moon.

mcqs.q: How many days in a synodic month (rounded)?
options: 30 days
36 days
21 days
27 days
